summary: Submitted a second, independent scenario check for unit-C-append-log-identity-consistency (action=check), keeping the same accepted obligation and binding. The plan and harness exercise the appendEntries early return I recorded as the second branch in map v3: in a protocol-version-2 follower a conflicting LogAddPeerDeprecated entry is stored successfully, then processConfigurationLogEntry fails to decode it, so the handler sets rpcErr and returns before setLastLog while the cached last log identity still names the index DeleteRange removed. The prerequisite config_entry_error (node n1, success false) admits the operation and the monitor observes error_path_probe with oracle accepted==true and identity node, so a rejection of the leader's next valid AppendEntries is a complete violating witness for the same responsibility. Construction guidance from a scratch copy of the captured source showed cached_index 3 against stored_index 2 (consistent=false) with the RPC returning the decode error, and the follow-up request rejected via GetLog on the removed index; that local run is construction knowledge only and formal evidence requires the trusted runner's clean-copy execution, which this submission requests. Legality grounding cites S-raft-appendentries/S-logstore, notes that the deprecated entry types are valid for older protocol versions and that with protocol version < 3 the LocalID must be the network address (the harness sets it), and records uncertainties (artificial undecodable payload, protocol-version-2 scope, single follower). Preflight returned valid:true against map v3; the three earlier findings and their reviews remain confirmed.
